note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

Each item carries release_notes / body (truncated) + a keyword dimension_hint (raw, NOT a verdict) — the FOLLOW-UP is to read these and judge what the change actually does and whether it improves the protocol at a fundamental level (consensus/scaling/security/economics/new capability) vs routine housekeeping. dev.release_notes:
v2.10.3 is a security and stability release on top of `v2.10.2`. It's the public release of `v2.10.3-priv`, which most validators and major RPC providers already run.

No hardfork, no database schema change, no resync required. Nodes can be upgraded one at a time, in any order.

## Highlights

- **Execution**: parallel (BlockSTM V2) balance reads are resolved correctly across a self-destruct boundary (#2403). Shared block caches are size-capped and per-tx code hashes memoized, which lowers importer memory under heavy keccak / ecrecover load. Log counting while tracing no longer copies logs (#2460).
- **Txpool**: pending chains stranded behind a head that can't be mined are evicted after `txpool.strandedlifetime`. Filtered addresses also apply to SetCode (type 4) authorizations. The pool signer is no longer swapped when `allow-unprotected-txs` is set (#2464).
- **Storage trie preload**: segmented BFS queue for the preload, plus optional address-cache persistence across restarts. On a mainnet sentry, preload on restart drops from about 1h25m to about 4s.
- **P2P**: static peers stay dialed across jails and full dynamic slots (#2438), and are kept out of the peer dropper.
- **RPC**: the execution slot is re-acquired between batch items, and the RPC execution pool request timeout from config is applied.
- **Heimdall client**: the configured request timeout is now honored (#2411).
- **Go toolchain 1.26.8**.

# Protocol Changes
* Repeated universal state init on an already initialized account now refunds the whole deposit. Previously the deposit also topped up storage staking. ([#16486](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16486))
* `UniversalStateInit` is accepted only in its canonical borsh encoding, so each state init has exactly one valid encoding and one account id. Enables the check behind the status of the `universal_state_init_to_account_id` host function and comes with fees that price the decode and canonical check. ([#16550](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16550))

# Non-protocol Changes
* `ReceiptPromiseInputSizeLimit` is enabled at protocol version 87 and effectively disabled at protocol version 88 (limit set to max value). ([#16561](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16561))
* Cold store loop stays alive on RocksDB 10 under stall limits, TTL, and compaction I/O. ([#16502](https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/16502))

# Protocol upgrade voting

This release upgrades the protocol version from 87 to 88.
Voting for protocol version 88 will start on Wednesday October 21st 00:00 UTC.
To continue participating in consensus, you need to upgrade your node before this time.

If voting succeeds in one epoch, the protocol upgrade to version 88 is expected to happen 7-14 hours after the voting epoch ends.

## Protocol
#### Sui Protocol Version in this release: `139`

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27989: Adds protocol version 139 with the `enable_forwarding_addresses` flag (devnet only). When enabled, the forwarding address registry is sequenced as an implicitly read system object and may be passed as a shared input.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28223: Protocol version 139 reduces the non-refundable storage fee from 1% to 0.01% of the storage rebate.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/27328: Under protocol version 131, random-beacon DKG that misses its timeout round now keeps running and can re-enable randomness mid-epoch if it completes, instead of disabling randomness for the whole epoch.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28233: On mainnet, protocol version 138 reduces the non-refundable storage fee from 1% to 0.01%.

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28224: Protocol version 139 charges non-system package inputs 1% of the per-byte object read cost.

## Nodes (Validators and Full nodes)

https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/28182: Full nodes that do not enable object or checkpoint pruning now drop `executed_transaction_digests` entries older than the previous epoch, bounding that table's disk and (on tidehunter) memory footprint. No action required.

# Hotfix Release

This is a private hotfix. The source code is not available yet. Please use the attached binaries or upgrade using the docker image.

## Who should upgrade

- **Validators**: YES
- **Fullnodes**: Recommended
- **Deposits & withdrawals**: No impact

Hotfix commit: `433c185c8e9c41205a83dfe289ac1072b7f00d1a`

> **ℹ️ This is not a mandatory upgrade, but we ask all `pacific-1` validators and node operators to update to `v6.7.1` before the FlatKV migration starts** (~17:00 UTC on 9 October 2026, when the migration proposal passes). `atlantic-2` has already migrated, so operators there can update at their convenience. There is no governance proposal and no coordinated chain halt for this update.

`v6.7.1` is a patch release on top of `v6.7.0`. It has eight fixes and one removal. Most fixes are for the EVM migration, which moves EVM state from memIAVL to FlatKV. Other fixes make state sync and `seid rollback` safer. `v6.7.1` also removes the deprecated `seid export` command.

| 🖥️ **RPC, full and archive nodes** | **Requested before the migration on `pacific-1`.** `v6.7.1` also fixes wrong contract nonces in the state store after state sync. |
| 🌐 **Networks** | `pacific-1` before the migration starts. `atlantic-2` at your convenience. |
| ⏱️ **Downtime** | The node stops only for one restart. There is no coordinated halt. |
| 🔗 **Compatibility** | There are no consensus-breaking changes, and the AppHash does not change. Nodes on `v6.7.0` and `v6.7.1` stay in consensus, so `v6.7.0` nodes do not halt, but they do not get the fixes below. |

governance.title: Should Starknet become an independent post-quantum L1?
governance.body:
On October 8th, StarkWare announced they are actively exploring the possibility of Starknet evolving into an independent post-quantum L1 with greater control over its own security. This non-binding poll seeks to gauge STRK holders’ interest in exploring that direction further.

A “Yes” vote indicates support for further research. It does not constitute approval of a transition to an L1.

For further context and discussion, please see: [https://community.starknet.io/t/should-starknet-become-an-independent-post-quantum-l1/116392](https://community.starknet.io/t/should-starknet-become-an-independent-post-quantum-l1/116392).

1.  Yes, this should be researched
    
2.  No, this shouldn't be researched
    
3.  Neutral, I need more information
    

Any future decision to proceed with a transition would be subject to a dedicated governance process.
